body: Correction/deepening from the repair work (2026-11-04 ~12:10 CST): the proxy retirement above was real, but the #3232 session's provider.auth 401s were NOT caused by the dead proxy — its turns never reached :18750 (no proxy journal entries). Verified root cause for those 401s: the session was created 2026-11-01 and its pinned provider resolution targets the retired base 'openai' provider. There is no credential row under integration_id 'openai' (the OAuth rows live under openai.main / openai.alternate, both active and healthy), so the server called api.openai.com with no Authorization header — the error body byte-matches api.openai.com's no-auth response. Fresh sessions on the current config resolve openai.main and succeed (verified end-to-end). The audit has been re-dispatched as a fresh session (ses_e5e583ee02affe3rm1LyXRfS70) and is running. The retirement-gate ask in this issue stands — the proxy was still serving live routes (scout/workhorse via the proxy path verified after restoration) when it was removed — but session-pinned stale provider references are a second, related hazard worth covering in the same gate: sessions created before a provider rename keep resolving to the retired id.

## Intake review

- **Related issues/PRs:** opencode#1153 (the retirement commit e8b4cdc75), opencode#1146 (the server-façade cutover that has not landed in deployed config), PR #5576 (closed the #3232 issue while its audit deliverable stayed outstanding). No duplicate: a search returns only this issue.
- **Notes:** Enriched by the fleet monitor (Duty 2, protocol §5): acceptance criteria appended, labels normalized (kind/infrastructure, priority/high, effort/m, source/human). The stopgap (restored proxy files + hand-placed user unit on the laptop, ~12:03 CST) is an operational bridge, not the fix — the owed work is the retirement gate plus a repo-managed end state.
- **Risks / suggested approach:** Gate shape: a deploy-time check that counts live routing references (52 `opencode-route` references in the deployed config at filing) and blocks removal of a component that still has references. Also disposition the burned #3232 audit deliverable explicitly so it does not stay silently owed.

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=fleet-monitor state=filed at=2026-11-04T18:29:09Z -->

## Switch gate resolved for the route-proxy retirement — live evidence 2026-11-04 ~18:40 CST

The switch-blocking question on this issue — *does anything still route through :18750?* — is answered **no**, on live reads (not records):

- Deployed config `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.jsonc`: **`18750` occurs 0 times.** No baseURL points at the route proxy. The 52 `opencode-route` hits are **model-id strings** (`"model": "opencode-route/workhorse"`, `small_model: opencode-route/speed`, agent model fields, demotion targets) — tier names now served natively by the server façade's in-server route provider (the config's own comment at the provider block: "by the server; no baseURL/apiKey (the provider owns auth)"). Same shape in the repo copy at origin/main (0× `18750`, 52× model-id refs) — deployed and repo agree.
- Other proxy baseURLs still present in the deployed config are exactly the doors that remain standing by design: :18747 muse-proxy (backend retained), :18748 commandcode-proxy, :18749 claude-code-proxy. :18744 (codex-proxy) and :18750 are absent.
- The OpenClaw consumer was rewired to the façade by PR #5588 (merged), and its hand-placed credential stand-in was retired earlier today with the full 5-step battery (opencode#1146 comment 6646057126).

So the deployed config **has** migrated to the server façade — the first of this issue's two acceptable end states — and a switch that deploys the repo state (no route-proxy unit/files in nix) removes nothing that anything references. The retirement gate question for THIS switch is resolved.

What remains open on this issue (not switch-blocking): (1) the general retirement-gate mechanism (the port-fallback guard exists; a config-reference gate for future door retirements is still owed); (2) removal of the vestigial stopgap artifacts — the hand-placed user unit `~/.config/systemd/user/opencode-route-proxy.service` (observed flapping in auto-restart earlier today; it serves a port nothing references) and the untracked restored `~/code/bin/opencode-route-proxy*` files — cleanup being executed/verified in this switch round's census; (3) the #3232 audit re-run/re-file.

## Live-state reconciliation — the route proxy is DOWN; the route ids are served by the server façade (2026-11-04 ~19:37 CST)

WS-E's flag (deployment epic #5765 / M1 #5768) prompted this live check. Findings, all read live on the laptop just now:

**The hand-placed stopgap unit is broken and looping.** `~/.config/systemd/user/opencode-route-proxy.service` (the 12:03 CST stopgap fragment): ActiveState was `activating/auto-restart`, **NRestarts 1478 and climbing** (1484 by the time I stopped it), ExecMainStatus **127** — its ExecStart target `/home/user/code/bin/opencode-route-proxy-start.sh` **no longer exists** (`~/code/bin/opencode-route-proxy*` is gone entirely; the untracked stopgap copies vanished when the `~/code` checkout moved to current main, where the program is retired).

**Nothing serves :18750, and nothing needs to.** No listener on 18750, no route-proxy process. There is no second instance and no live twin beside the stale unit — the contradiction resolves as: *a vestigial hand unit flapping against a deleted script, while the work moved in-server.* The deployed config references the port zero times (gate record, comment 6646298767).

**Serving verification — the `opencode-route/*` ids are live on the façade.** Against the standing server on 127.0.0.1:13420: authenticated `GET /v1/models` → 200 (28 leaf/provider models; route ids are not listed there — they are internal tier ids), unauthenticated → 401, and `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"model":"opencode-route/scout"` → **HTTP 200**, a real completion object echoing the route model with usage (54 prompt / 20 completion tokens). The in-server route provider serves the tiers; the standalone proxy carries no traffic because there is no proxy and no config path to one.

**Action taken (this issue's resolution scope):** `systemctl --user stop opencode-route-proxy.service` — now `inactive/dead`, restart counter frozen. The fragment file was **left in place** and the unit is still `enabled`: it will re-flap at the next user-manager start until the fragment is removed. That removal is the deployment track's (epic #5765, M1 #5768) — flagging it here rather than taking it, since the switch round that was to deploy the repo's proxy-free state is gated on code#5736.

**Net for this issue:** the switch-blocking question stays resolved — now stronger: the proxy is not merely unreferenced, it is *down*, and the fleet's route traffic demonstrably flows through the server façade. Remaining on #5610: the general retirement-gate mechanism, the stopgap-fragment removal (via #5768 / the gated switch re-run), and the #3232 audit re-file.

Wire it into the unit-removal path (the nix/home module or the decommission recipe) and add a shell/PBT-free unit test with a positive (references present → fail) and negative (no references → pass) case. Acceptance: removing a route/provider with references present exits non-zero.

Resolve the interim state one way: either restore `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` + `-start.sh` and a **repo-managed** unit (no hand-placed unit) until the façade cutover changes the deployed config, or complete opencode#1154's cutover so the deployed config stops naming `opencode-route` at all. The current state — neither proxy nor cutover — is the one option that leaves the gate red and the config broken.
3. The #3232 receipt-validation audit deliverable stays owed; re-run or re-file it after (2) resolves.
